sections.title: Site Appearance
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to help you brand and customize the Marketplace:
1. by determining your marketplace name
2. by loading your organization’s logo’s
3. by specifying your organization’s colors
4. by changing terms in the marketplace to match the terms you use today
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: An organization has many options to customize their Marketplace. Site branding can take some time to determine, so we encourage you to start thinking of that now. It is very helpful to have your site and project branded so that you can build its identity early on.

Part of developing site’s identity includes the organization message, marketplace contact information, and organization logo. These will all display on the homepage. A logo can also be displayed on the log in page. In addition, the organization message provides an excellent way to send a message to users regarding the Marketplace, its suppliers, or any information that is relevant to them.

Often, organizations have their own terms that differ from default field terms in the Marketplace. For example, where the application refers to Suppliers, your organization may use the term Vendors. These terms can be relabeled through-out the Marketplace to allow your end users to be more comfortable with their shopping experience.

sections.title: Users
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to help you identify:
1. who will be using the Marketplace
2. how each user will access the Marketplace
3. what access each user will have in the Marketplace
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: Each user who needs access to the Marketplace is assigned a unique user profile. Users log in to the Marketplace using a URL in a standard web browser. Or, depending on the integrations that are in scope for your project users log in by clicking a link on a portal within your organization. The user is also assigned roles which determine the level of access he or she has once they login to the site. Roles are created within the Marketplace to manage users with similar permissions. The JAGGAER Marketplace allows users with the correct permissions to save commonly used information to their profile or to change their personal information and preferences.

Examples: Each Marketplace has six standard roles. Examples are: Shopper, Requestor, Approver, Purchasing, Accounts Payable, and System Administrator. Clients may create additional roles or sub roles. A client may also choose not to use all five roles.
Shopper: These users can shop for items, but cannot submit a cart
Requestor: These users can shop for items and submit carts that they created or carts that were assigned to them from a shopper
Approver: These users can review (approve, return, or reject) purchase requestors that are assigned to them
Purchasing These users can make changes to purchase orders
Accounts Payable: These users are responsible for the day to day processing of invoices
Administrator: These users can make changes to site configuration, user information, suppliers, etc.

sections.title: Contract
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to help you identify:
1. the number of contracts to be loaded in the Marketplace for go live
2. if approval is required for certain contract purchases
3. are there contract maximums or spending limits
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: Contract Manager Module of Spend Direct Enterprise provides a centralized repository for electronic contracts. This module integrates with the e-procurement process to improve contract visibility, tracking and analysis. End users search contracts and view key information about them, reference contract numbers on requisitions, purchase orders, and invoices, and can choose to apply special contract pricing to items in their shopping carts. Contract owners, or other stakeholders, can be notified of key contract dates and financial milestones to more efficiently manage their contracts.
Examples: Scenarios for Contract Management in Spend Director Enterprise

Your organization has a contract for Office Supplies that should be fully viewable by all users and all users should be able to “use it.” In addition, whenever someone orders from this supplier, it should automatically assign to this contract for all products purchased.
My organization has an agreement with a vendor for a small set of products that is available to all users. This vendor does not provide a catalog; the available products are listed on the contract.

My organization has an agreement with a janitorial supplies vendor for light bulbs, but no other products. I also want to audit a vendors catalog by tracking the pricing of the top 10 light bulb purchases. This contract is available to a single department and is only applicable if purchased from a specific location.

sections.title: Shopping
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to help you define the users’ shopping experience:
1. for purchasing goods and services
2. for defining preferred suppliers
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: Configurations can be made in the site to control what your users are seeing in the Marketplace and to identify key relationships with your suppliers. Suppliers can be classified and given preferred positioning in product search results. In addition, your organization can have personalized control of who has access to procure certain items in the system. Some configurations are only available if your Marketplace is using a specific catalog type. If restrictions and supplier preferences are needed, discuss them with your implementation team.

In addition to shopping the catalogs, users may also place non-catalog orders in the Marketplace. Non-catalog items are those that are not from a hosted or punch-out catalog. These orders can be placed with enabled suppliers or other suppliers who are not enabled. For example, you may order business cards from a local printing shop, or place catering orders with a local restaurant. Non-catalog requests can be entered using a custom JAGGAER form or by using the non-catalog ordering screen. Custom forms are typically used when additional data needs to be collected for a purchase order and/or special approval is required prior to creating the purchase order.

Examples: The U-shop Marketplace has four catalogs from furniture suppliers. Ordering furniture requires an authorization process outside of the marketplace before the item (s) can be ordered. Only 2 people are allowed to place orders with furniture suppliers in the marketplace. These catalogs should not be visible to all requestors.

sections.title: Requisition Workflow
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to:
1. Define the fields or data that is required as part of the check-out process
2. Understand what is required to configure the requisition workflow in the Marketplace
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: The workflow process begins when a cart is submitted and continues through when the purchase order is sent out to the supplier. The two major phases of workflow are Purchase Requisition workflow and Purchase Order Workflow.

The Purchase Order Workflow are automated system steps that are used to send the Purchase Order to the vendor as well as to export the Purchase Order Data to the ERP if necessary. There may also be steps for error handling and for Purchase Order Revisions. The focus during implementation is to define workflow for Marketplace requisitions.

The design of an organization’s workflow varies from simple to complex depending on the business needs and purchasing practices. The goal of workflow is to make sure that all orders sent out are valid. For example, workflow may involve financial approvals. In other cases, it may verify that certain types of items (such as radioactive or other hazardous items) that are ordered through the system follow the correct approval process based on your business process. Certain organizations require the purchasing department to approve all orders sent out, while other organizations may have departmental approval only or special handling based on line items or the amounts.

sections.title: Invoices
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to help you:
1. Define who will be entering invoices in the marketplace
2. Define tolerances
3. Define invoice routing/workflow
4. Define general invoicing configuration that is required
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: The Invoicing Module allows an automated, streamlined receiving and invoice process by allowing users to enter receipts and/or invoices against purchase orders. Using the receiving functionality is optional but allows clients to take advantage of the robust matching capabilities that are available in the Marketplace. The overall goal of the invoicing process in the Marketplace is to help your organization identify invoices that are payable. This goal is achieved through defining tolerances at the organization level or at the supplier level. In the cases where the invoice is within tolerances, or it matches the Purchase Order and the receipt, the system automatically flags the invoice as being payable or OK to Pay. There is limited interaction from the AP Staff. In the cases where the documents do not match or they are out of tolerance, then AP Staff needs to investigate these issues in order to flag the invoice as payable.

sections.title: Suppliers
paragraphs: Goal: The goal of this section is to help you define:
1. Catalog suppliers for the Marketplace
2. A standardized Ship to address format for your shipping labels
3. Billing addresses to be used in the Marketplace
Instructions: Complete the Solution Configuration section after you have reviewed the concepts and examples below.

Concepts: Suppliers enabled during your implementation will provide items via an electronic catalog. The catalog can either be in a hosted or punch-out format; each offers unique features to meet your organization’s needs. Your implementation team will discuss the benefits of each with your organization. When identifying the initial suppliers for go live consider your suppliers who have the highest volume and spend and ensure all verticals are covered to meet the needs of each end user group at go live. For example, you may want an office supply vendor as well as a computer or IT equipment supplier.

Billing and Shipping addresses are a key part of your Marketplace configuration because they determine who is billed for a purchase and that products are successfully delivered in a timely manner. The formats for these addresses should always be consistent and abbreviated whenever possible.

sections.title: Solution Configuration
paragraphs: 1. Provide a list of top your 15 suppliers you would like to enable. For short projects, expect to go live with 8-10 suppliers (or more if catalog only enablements).

Consideration: Spend, transaction volume, go-live departments, contract status, and state mandated contracts are some criteria that may considered to identify suppliers. sections.title: Objectives
paragraphs: This document is meant to provide recommended ways of implementing Change Order processes within the JAGGAER e-Procurement application.

sections.title: Definitions
paragraphs: Change Order: Defined as having to modify a Purchase Order to have the correct accounting information, quantities, prices and items that will be received and/or invoiced.
MarketPlace: Your JAGGAER e-Procurement application
ERP: Your Enterprise Resource Planning application

sections.title: Consideration
paragraphs: Due to the complexity of modifying Purchase Orders, business policies should be put in place to minimize the use of Change Orders. It is highly recommended that the Change Order process be managed by Purchasing, with Purchasing reviewing, approving and completing the Purchase Order (Change Order) modifications. When developing a Change Order process, scrutinize the possible scenarios to determine if a Change Order is the correct, most efficient solution.

sections.title: Facilitate Settlement:
paragraphs: For clients using Invoicing/Matching on Marketplace, it is recommended that a Change Order process be established so that Purchase Orders can be modified (i.e. changed) to facilitate the matching process. If Invoice/Matching is not part of the Marketplace solution, Change Orders are not typically required.

sections.title: Re-distribute Purchase Orders:
paragraphs: Using a Change Order to modify the amount/quantity on a PO and re-distribute the PO to the Supplier is discouraged due to the following factors; Suppliers may not have a process in place to accept a PO change, Often the original order has already processed by the time a PO change is initiated and the inherent risk of duplicating an order.

sections.title: Keeping the ERP and Marketplace in sync:
paragraphs: Change Orders can be used to keep PO data in sync between the ERP and Marketplace. Not keeping the two systems in sync will lessen the validity of reporting from the Marketplace, however it is important to weigh whether reporting alone justifies the effort involved.

sections.title: A. For Purchase Orders that originate on the JAGGAER Marketplace
General Process/Prerequisites:
paragraphs: 1. Users will not change POs directly. They will use a form to communicate the change(s) needed, Financial Approval can be required and if valid, Purchasing will be responsible for completing the changes.
2. A Change Order form is created on the Marketplace to allow users to request Purchase Order changes
3. The form allows the user to enter the PO number, change description (free text field), new PO amount and type of change(s) required (pull-down or checkboxes)

4. Type of change required is a pull-down or checkbox selection that allows for a user to select 1 more items to change. Ex: Increase amount, add line, change accounting information, cancel Purchase Order
5. Change Order forms are completed, added to a cart and submitted by Users
6. Change Order forms cannot be mixed in the cart with any other item.
7. Requisition workflow on the Marketplace will be such that;
8. Change Order Requisitions may require Financial Approval, routing to Approvers based on the change being requested (i.e. Increase dollar amount) and Requisition data.
9. Change Order Requisitions that are valid will stop for purchasing approval or action as the final Workflow step.
10. Change Order Requisitions will not “create” Purchase Orders
11. Change Order Requests will be reviewed and acted on by Purchasing as part of the workflow/approval process.
12. Invalid Change Order requests will be rejected or returned to the User.
13. For valid Change Orders, reference recommended solutions below

sections.title: Recommendation 1: Purchasing modifies POs manually in both JAGGAER Marketplace and ERP (JAGGAER recommended)
paragraphs: 1. Valid Change Order requests will be completed on the Marketplace and the ERP by modifying the referenced Purchase Order accordingly in both systems. For the Marketplace PO:
2. Modifications are made/saved on the Marketplace PO
3. The “Finalize Revision” Action is invoked, creating a Marketplace PO revision.
4. Once the Purchase Order modifications have been completed, the Change Order Requisition is approved/completed.

sections.title: Recommendation 2: Purchasing modifies PO in JAGGAER Marketplace. PO revisions are integrated with ERP. This recommendation requires a compatible integration.
paragraphs: 1. Valid Change Order requests will be completed on the Marketplace by modifying the referenced Purchase Order accordingly.
2. Modifications are made/saved on the Marketplace PO
3. The “Finalize Revision” Action is invoked with the “Resend to…”ERP PO Export option checked/on.
4. Once the Purchase Order modifications have been completed, the Change Order Requisition is approved/completed.

sections.title: Objectives
paragraphs: 1. Procurement organizations that look to conduct business in a fair and equitable manner use a competitive bidding process to procure goods and/or services. Typically there is a dollar amount above which the organization is required to initiate their competitive bidding process.

sections.title: Definitions
paragraphs: 1. None

sections.title: Considerations
paragraphs: 1. The following recommendations are only applicable if the client is using Requisition Manager.

2. Client policy and dollar thresholds dictate the recommendation or combination of recommendations to handle the bidding process. For example, end users are allowed to obtain quotes below a certain dollar amount. While if the requisition exceeds the dollar threshold, the purchasing department has to complete the bid process for requisitions.

sections.title: Scenario 1: Purchasing Policy requires the requisitioner to obtain a number of quotes for their item for orders meeting a specific dollar threshold. The order is placed with the lowest bidder.
paragraphs: Recommendation:

1. The end user works with the identified suppliers to obtain a quote for their item (s) outside of the marketplace. Once the supplier is identified, the end user logs into the Marketplace to place a non-catalog order to the supplier of their item (s). The quotes that were obtained can be attached as internal attachments and an internal note saying that the attachments are other supplier quotes. The quote for the order is attached as an external attachment along with an external note to the supplier. Typically, workflow is configured to require an approval for non-catalog orders, so these types of request are usually reviewed.

sections.title: Scenario 2: Purchasing Policy requires the Purchasing Department to complete a bid process for orders exceeding a specific dollar threshold.
paragraphs: Recommendation:

1. If the organization's policy is that the Purchasing Department has to initiate the bid process, then a Bid Request Form is created for use in the Marketplace. If the end user knows their item requires bidding he or she completes the form and submits the Bid Request Form to Purchasing. The Purchasing Department completes the bidding process and notifies the end user that a supplier has been identified. The end user submits a non-catalog requisition to the identified supplier for goods or services to be procured. The requisition routes through workflow for approvals as required.

2. In cases where the end user does not know that the item requires bidding and he or she has submitted a requisition, the Purchasing Department is able to review the requisition and conduct the bidding process outside of the Marketplace. Clients can determine how the bid award should be handled, i.e. the requestor is notified and he or she must submit a new requisition with the updated supplier and price of the item (s). Or, Purchasing updates the requisition with the new supplier and price or the item (s).

sections.title: Scenario 3: The Requisitioner needs to purchase an item and knows that their item requires bidding because it exceeds the dollar threshold stated in the purchasing policy. The vendor is unknown when the user is entering their non-catalog requisition.
paragraphs: Recommendation:

1. Some organizations allow an end user to submit a requisition even though the vendor has not yet been identified. In this case, there are setup requirements in the Marketplace to facilitate these requests. This requires configuring the marketplace to allow users to submit a non-catalog requisition without a supplier or using a "dummy" supplier profile (e.g. Supplier Name = TBD, Bid Vendor). Workflow is configured to route all requisitions without a vendor or vendors who have this supplier name to Purchasing for review. Purchasing conducts the bidding process outside of the Marketplace and determines the vendor that will provide the goods or services. Purchasing updates the supplier and price on the requisition and the requisition routes through workflow for financial approval.

sections.title: Objective
paragraphs: 1. This document is meant to provide recommended options for implementing Fiscal Year End processes within the JAGGAER e-Procurement application.

sections.title: Definitions
paragraphs: Fiscal Year: A fiscal year is any 52-week period used consistently by an organization for the purposes of financial reporting and policy setting. It may or may not correspond with the typical calendar year of January to December. Organizations may choose to designate a different time period as its fiscal year as a way of recognizing seasonal variations in its business, as a method of minimizing its tax burden, or for any number of other reasons.
Fiscal Year End: The completion of the Fiscal Year.
Marketplace: Your JAGGAER e-Procurement application

sections.title: Considerations
paragraphs: 1. While a Fiscal Year can be any 52-week period, Higher Education and State Government organizations typically begin their Fiscal Year on July 1st while Commercial/Businesses begin on January 1st.
2. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) requires that all financial and accounting transactions be recorded in the Fiscal Year in which they are made.

3. Organizations should have a Fiscal Year End Close-out process established with procedures specific to their accounting/procurement systems as well as document processing deadlines and closing dates that are published to Users. The Fiscal Year End Close-out process may also include; Different document processing deadlines based on amount or purchase type, an Accounts Payable “window” for submitting Year End Invoices and/or specific system instructions for Users on submitting orders for the new Fiscal Year as well as budget considerations.
4. The intent of this document is to provide recommendations specifically for the JAGGAER e-Procurement application (Marketplace). All recommendations should be carefully scrutinized to ensure:
5. The best fit with your established Fiscal Year End Close-out process.
6. Compatibility with any external system processing and integrations.
7. Efficiency and effectiveness based on your Marketplace modules.

sections.title: General Process/Prerequisites for all Recommended Solutions:
paragraphs: 1. Purchase Order and/or Invoice processing deadlines for Fiscal Year End should be published for Marketplace Users. This can be accomplished on Marketplace using the “Message Board”, “Send Email To Users” or the “Site Terms and Conditions”.

2. When practical, Organizations are encouraged to setup a Purchasing administrated website to publish Fiscal Year End; procedures and policies, processing deadlines and Frequently Ask Questions (FAQs).
3. Blanket/Standing Orders: Organizations should follow established policies for handling Blanket/Standing Orders during Fiscal Year End.

sections.title: A. “Shutting Down” Current Year JAGGAER Marketplace Requisitions
paragraphs: Organizations may choose to mandate a “Shut Down” period where any new Requisitions submitted during this time are held for review. Organizations may allow Users to place orders for the New Fiscal Year during this period and review those separately.
This is accomplished using the Requisition “Accounting Date” and Requisition Workflow to evaluate orders based on that date.
Example Fiscal Year End is June 30th. Current Year ordering is “Shut Down” on June 15th. Orders for the New Fiscal Year (> July 1st) are allowed but will be “held” for review.

This requires the “Auto-populate Accounting Date” parameter to be enabled on the Requisition document. Enabling this parameter will automatically populate the Accounting Date on the Requisition with the date it was submitted. If not already enabled, this parameter can be turned on at the start of the “Shut Down” period by finalizing and activating a new document version.
Requisition Workflow Steps:

1. Whenever possible Advanced Dynamic Workflow (ADW) should be used to create these workflow steps in order to give the System Administrator full control of the process. If these steps require the checking of advanced criteria, the workflow may need to be hardcoded, requiring SQ Support to “activate” the workflow each year.
2. Fiscal Year workflow steps would be “activated” at the start of the “Shut Down” period and “inactivated” when the Fiscal Year rollover is complete.
“Fiscal Year Orders” ADW step: Sends any Requisitions with an Accounting Date earlier than July 1stto a workflow folder for review by Purchasing. The Approver can:
1. Approve (i.e. emergency orders)
2. Change the Accounting Date to later than July 1st and Approve
3. Reject the Requisition
“New Fiscal Year Orders” ADW step: Sends any Requisitions with an Accounting Date later than July 1stto a workflow folder for review by Purchasing/Buyers.
1. Users would need to be trained on placing New Fiscal Year orders, by editing the “Accounting Date” to July 1st or later during the Checkout process.
2. The workflow Approvers (Purchasing or Buyers) can review and approve these Requisitions once all systems are ready for New Fiscal Year processing.
3. NOTE: This step can be omitted for the Requisition and the New Fiscal Year Order can be held at the Purchase Order stage. See: B. “Holding” New Fiscal Year JAGGAER Marketplace Purchase Orders
Once the New Fiscal Year rollover is complete and budgets are open, the Fiscal Year related workflow steps can be inactivated (as well as the “Auto-populate Accounting Date” parameter if necessary.)

sections.title: B. “Holding” New Fiscal Year JAGGAER Marketplace Purchase Orders
paragraphs: Organizations may choose to allow Requisition processing for New Fiscal Year orders and “hold” the resulting Purchase Order until the Fiscal Year rollover is complete. New Fiscal Year Requisitions are processed, however the resulting Purchase Order is held prior to the revision stage (or “Purchase Order Create” for Banner).
This is accomplished using the Requisition “Accounting Date” and Purchase Order Workflow to evaluate Purchase Orders based on the Requisition Accounting Date.

This requires the “Auto-populate Accounting Date” parameter to be enabled on the Requisition document. Enabling this parameter will automatically populate the Accounting Date on the Requisition with the date it was submitted. If not already enabled, this parameter can be turned on at the start of the “Shut Down” period by finalizing and activating a new document version.
Purchase Order Workflow Steps:

1. Whenever possible Advanced Dynamic Workflow (ADW) should be used to create the workflow step in order to give the System Administrator full control of the process. If the step requires the checking of advanced criteria, the workflow may need to be hardcoded, requiring SQ Support to “activate” the workflow each year.
2. Fiscal Year workflow steps would be “activated” at the start of the “Shut Down” period and “inactivated” when the Fiscal Year rollover is complete.
“New Fiscal Year Orders” ADW step: Sends any Purchase Order with an Accounting Date later than July 1stto a workflow folder for review by Purchasing.
1. Users would need to be trained on placing New Fiscal Year orders, by editing the “Accounting Date” to July 1st or later during the Requisition Checkout process.
2. The “New Fiscal Year Orders” Purchase Order workflow step would hold the Purchase Order prior to the revision (or “Purchase Order Create” for Banner) step.
3. The workflow Approvers can review and Approve these Purchase Orders once all systems are ready for New Fiscal Year processing.
Once the New Fiscal Year rollover is complete and budgets are open, the Fiscal Year related workflow steps can be inactivated (as well as the “Auto-populate Accounting Date” parameter if necessary.)

sections.title: C. “Holding” JAGGAER Marketplace Invoices during Fiscal Year Cutover
paragraphs: Organizations may choose to “hold” Marketplace Invoice and Credits during their Fiscal Year cutover. Preventing Invoices and Credits from processing through workflow during the cutover:
1. Allows Accounts Payable/Purchasing to review these Marketplace documents to ensure that the charges/credits align with the Fiscal year in which the goods were received or services performed.
2. Can be used to hold Invoices/Credits while the ERP is unavailable during the cutover.

This is accomplished using the Invoice “Accounting Date” which is populated with the date the draft Invoice/Credit memo is created and Invoice Workflow to evaluate the documents based on that Accounting Date.
Example

Fiscal Year End is June 30th. Invoice cutover has been defined by the Organization as June 15th to July 15th. Fiscal year Invoice workflow will be enabled during this period to ensure that goods not delivered/services not performed until after June 30th will be charged/credited to next year’s budget while charges/credits for goods and services on or before June 30th are applied to the current Fiscal Year.
1. This uses the “Accounting Date” on the Invoice/Credit Memo which is pre-populated with the date the draft document was created.
2. Invoice Workflow Steps:

3. Whenever possible Advanced Dynamic Workflow (ADW) should be used to create the workflow step in order to give the System Administrator full control of the process. If the step requires the checking of advanced criteria, the workflow may need to be hardcoded, requiring SQ Support to “activate” the workflow each year.
4. Fiscal Year workflow steps would be “activated” at the start of the “Cutover” period and “inactivated” when the Fiscal Year rollover is complete.

5. “Fiscal Year Cutover” ADW step: Sends any Invoice/Credit Memo with an Accounting Date between June 15th and July 15th(from above example) to a workflow folder for review by Accounts Payable/Purchasing.
6. The “Fiscal Year Cutover” Invoice workflow step would hold the Invoice/Credit Memo at the start of Invoice workflow to limit match exceptions and any other approval/review steps.

7. The workflow Approvers can review these documents based on when the goods/services will be received to either allow the document to continue (with or without edits) or hold the documents until after all systems are ready for New Fiscal Year processing (cutover complete).
8. Once the New Fiscal Year cutover is complete, the Invoice Fiscal Year related workflow step(s) can be inactivated or updated to evaluate for the next Fiscal Year Cutover.

sections.title: Objective
paragraphs: 1. Clients can use their JAGGAER Marketplace to procure services like consulting, maintenance services, or printing. The services that are procured may be performed by suppliers that are external to the organization but there are also instances where the services needed may be performed by an internal department in the organization. Examples of internal service requests are printing, catering, IT or maintenance requests.

sections.title: Definitions
paragraphs: 1. Form - customizable component of the Marketplace application that is used to collect additional information that is not available on the non-catalog item or part of the checkout process.

sections.title: Consideration
paragraphs: 1. Clients who are not using Requisition Manager are unable to use forms in as described in the solutions below.
2. Spend Director/Order Manager (Sandwich) Clients can use the non-catalog item to initiate the requisition for service and complete the process in their ERP.
3. When using forms in the Marketplace, only the following fields are transferred to the ERP: Supplier, Product Description, Quantity, UOM, Commodity Code, and Unit Price.
4. All clients can use the non-catalog item if specific information for a purchase does not need to be collected.

sections.title: Scenario 1: One time service where specific information is required
paragraphs: Recommendation:

1. A custom form is typically used to gather specific requests. The form may be configured with the preferred or specific supplier for that service. Using a form allows the client to drive end users to a specific services supplier and it also allows the organization to capture the correct information for that purchase. There are some instances where the service that is being procured requires a special approval prior to creating the purchase order. In these cases, the form is routed to a special form approver for their review.
2. Examples: Moving Services, Catering Services, Guest Lecturer

sections.title: Scenario 2: An organization that wants to collect specific information regarding a type of service where multiple invoices are expected (i.e. a blanket) from an external supplier, a custom form is typically used to handle specific requests.
paragraphs: Recommendation:

1. The form may be configured with the preferred or specific supplier for that service. Using a form allows the client to drive end users to a specific services supplier and it also allows the organization to capture the correct information for that purchase. There are some instances where the service that is being procured requires a special approval prior to creating the purchase order. In these cases, the form is routed to a special form approver for their review.

2. If the client has Settlement and multiple invoices are expected (e.g. blankets), then the form is used to trigger workflow to draw down the purchase order amount. The purchase order remains open until the purchase amount is reached and disregards the quantity received. The end user creates a cost receipt to track the services rendered as invoices are received.

3. For organizations using spend director enterprise, a contract can be created with a form associated to the contract. This method allows the client to use some of the contract manager features like tracking spend and notification tiers against a defined Purchase Order (budget) each time the form is used
4. Examples include: Landscaping Services, Cleaning Services, Copy Machine Maintenance, etc.

In cases where a purchase order is created for distribution to an external supplier, the form can be faxed or emailed to the supplier. This includes suppliers who are setup for fax, email and electronic delivery.

Scenario 3: Similarly, an organization that wants to collect specific information regarding a type of service that will be performed by an internal supplier typically uses a form for these internal service requests.
Recommendation:

1. A form is typically used to handle specific internal requests. The form is setup with the preferred or specific supplier for that service. Using the form allows the organization to capture the correct information for this service request. For these types of requests, a purchase order is generated and sent to the internal department. Examples are Catering or Printing Services. In some cases, a purchase order is not generated and the form is routed to an approver who will use the information on the form to complete the request. Examples are IT Request or Maintenance/Work Order Request. In either case, when the purchase order or the form is received, the requestor is contacted to schedule the service.
2. Examples of internal services include: Work Order Request, IT request – New user account setup, hardware installation
